grh_e2135a8b8235579295dd.title: Action -Berry Kroeger
paragraphs: After suffering symptoms he believes are the beginning of a disabling stroke, 52-year-old Christopher Bell secretly gives up his business and attempts to make his death look like a mountaineering accident on a nearly impossible Swiss glacier. At the point of exhaustion he hears another climber in danger and finds strength he thought was gone, rescuing a woman and reaching safety. The woman later tells Bell that she too had intended to die because of an incurable condition and proposes that each keep living for the other's sake. Her physician husband then reveals she is a talented actress, implying the encounter was deliberately arranged to restore Bell's reason to live.

This [[show|escape|Escape]] broadcast aired on April 4, 1948. It is listed as episode 35 in the archive. [[org|org.8480b75bc0c36e4b|CBS Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes Luis Van Rooten, Joseph Kearns, Berry Kroeger, Raymond Lawrence, and Erik Rolf. Other credited names include Norman Macdonnell as director, Norman Macdonnell as producer, Les Crutchfield as radio adaptor, and Roy Rowan as announcer.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.escape.b3ba65c253862d31|Action]]. Charles Montague is credited as author and Les Crutchfield adapted it for radio.

grh_e2dc8259ab8a30160bf5.title: George Washington Carver
paragraphs: A biographical dramatization traces George Washington Carver from a child born into slavery to the scientist and teacher who transformed agricultural research at Tuskegee Institute. Carver pursues education despite poverty and racism, then accepts Booker T. Washington's invitation to Alabama, where he builds a laboratory from discarded materials and attacks the South's dependence on cotton. His experiments with crops such as peanuts and sweet potatoes create new uses for depleted land and help poor farmers diversify. Framed as a tribute on Abraham Lincoln's birthday, the program presents Carver's life as proof that talent and service are not determined by race.

This [[show|words-at-war|Words at War]] broadcast aired on February 8, 1944. [[org|org.f2f0561f0ce2ddc5|NBC Radio Network]] carried the broadcast. The cast includes The Juanita Hall Singers, Fredric March, and Canada Lee. Other credited names include Anton M. Leader as director, Richard McDonagh as radio adaptor, and Jack Costello as host.
The surviving recording runs about 30 minutes.
This version dramatizes [[work|work.words.4fa8fec17d18fdc6|George Washington Carver]]. Rackham Holt is credited as author and Richard McDonagh adapted it for radio.

grh_e21160f08b3abaacd88d.title: Having a Wonderful Crime
paragraphs: Newlyweds Jake and Helene Justice cannot stop playing amateur detective, so criminal attorney Michael J. Malone reluctantly joins their honeymoon trip after a magician mysteriously disappears during his act. At a lakeside lodge, Jake and Helene find the magician Fred King dead inside a trunk that has been mistakenly delivered to Malone's room. Malone traces the killing to hotel manager Winslow, who murdered King while trying to recover a $50,000 check and then offers Malone money to stay quiet; instead Malone exposes the crime and once again solves the case his friends dragged him into.
